mainTopic: Courts of fewer than three judges: רבי אבהו's view, a judge's mistakes (טעה בדבר משנה vs. שיקול הדעת), and how many judges a פשרה needs and whether it requires a קנין.
overview: The גמרא has been explaining שמואל, who says a ruling by two judges is valid after the fact. An objection comes from רבי אבהו, who says everyone, even רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, holds that two judges' ruling is invalid. The גמרא answers that one אמורא may simply disagree with another. It then examines רבי אבהו's statement. רבי אבא challenges it from a משנה where a single judge's mistaken ruling stands. The גמרא answers that the litigants accepted that judge. He still pays because they asked him to judge by דין תורה. רב ספרא shows that the mistake must be in שיקול הדעת and not against an explicit משנה. רב פפא defines that as ruling against common practice where no הלכה was stated. Next, the גמרא asks whether the two-judge question is an argument between תנאים about ביצוע and פשרה. It concludes that they only argue whether פשרה is compared to דין, and that the view requiring two judges wants them only as witnesses. רב אשי infers that a פשרה does not need a קנין, but the הלכה is that it does. The amud ends with a new ברייתא: ביצוע needs three judges, just like דין.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי אבהו says everyone rejects a court of two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא considers saying that the רבנן disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, so שמואל would follow only רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. It then objects from רבי אבהו, who says that everyone, including רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, holds that two judges' ruling is invalid.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say that the רבנן disagree with רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, look, רבי אבהו says: two judges who judged, according to everyone their ruling is not a valid ruling!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a challenge to its explanation of שמואל. It points to רבי אבהו, who says everyone agrees a ruling by two judges does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל says two judges' ruling is valid after the fact. Someone might say the רבנן disagree, so שמואל follows only רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. But רבי אבהו says 'לדברי הכל': both רבן שמעון בן גמליאל and the רבנן hold that two judges' ruling is invalid. That leaves no תנא at all for שמואל to follow.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say (introduces a possible argument)
They disagree
According to everyone
Their ruling is not a valid ruling

phrases.english: And if you would say: the Rabbis disagree
with Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
but doesn't Rabbi Abbahu say:
two judges who judged a case —
according to everyone, their judgment is not a valid judgment!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: פְּלִיגִי רַבָּנַן עֲלֵיהּ דְּרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל, וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of שמואל's ruling about two judges.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that two judges' ruling is valid, and the attempt to base it on רבן שמעון בן גמליאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אבהו says that according to everyone, including רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, two judges' ruling is invalid. So שמואל has no תנא to rely on.

steps.title: Answer: you are setting one אמורא against another
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back the challenge. רבי אבהו is just one אמורא, and שמואל can see the רבנן's view differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are you throwing one man's statement against another man's statement?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the challenge. רבי אבהו's opinion does not bind שמואל, so it cannot disprove him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אבהו and שמואל are both אמוראים, and each may explain the רבנן his own way. רבי אבהו says everyone rejects two judges. שמואל holds the רבנן accept two judges' ruling after the fact. Quoting one does not disprove the other.

keyTerms.meaning: A man against a man (one אמורא against another)
You are throwing / contrasting

steps.whatToRemember: An אמורא's statement cannot refute another אמורא of equal standing. They may simply disagree.

phrases.english: Are you setting one man against another man?
phrases.notes: He means: רבי אבהו and שמואל are both אמוראים, so they can just disagree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the challenge of step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole challenge from רבי אבהו against שמואל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The challenge assumes one אמורא's opinion binds another, but אמוראים can disagree.

steps.title: רבי אבהו's statement quoted on its own
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now turns to רבי אבהו's statement itself: two judges who judged money cases made an invalid ruling, by everyone's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now the matter itself. רבי אבהו said: two judges who judged money cases, according to everyone their ruling is not a valid ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about רבי אבהו's statement, which came up in passing. This sets up the challenge that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'גופא' tells us the גמרא is now studying the statement for its own sake. This time it adds 'דיני ממונות', so it covers all money cases. Everyone agrees that two judges cannot make a binding ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: The matter itself (now studying a statement quoted earlier)
Money cases
Who judged

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a pointless repeat of step 1. 'גופא' means the גמרא now examines רבי אבהו's statement directly, and it is about to be challenged.

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rabbi Abbahu said:
two judges who judged money cases —
according to everyone, their judgment is not a valid judgment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבי אבהו's statement, quoted in step 1, and makes it the new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ruling by two judges in money cases is invalid, according to everyone.

steps.title: רבי אבא challenges from a משנה about one judge
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא quotes a משנה. A judge who ruled wrongly still has his ruling stand, and he pays from his own pocket. That suggests even one judge's ruling is valid.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא challenged רבי אבהו: if someone judged a case and let off the one who should pay, or made liable the one who should be free, or called pure something impure, or impure something pure, what he did stays done, and he pays from his own house.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא attacks רבי אבהו using a משנה. In that משנה, a single judge's mistaken ruling stays in force.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even one judge's ruling 'stays done', then a judge's ruling clearly counts even without three judges. That seems to contradict רבי אבהו, who says even two judges' ruling is invalid. The judge pays from his own pocket because he caused a loss.

keyTerms.meaning: He declared free the one who should pay
What he did stays done
He pays from his own house (his own money)

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba raised an objection to Rabbi Abbahu:

phrases.aramaic: דָּן אֶת הַדִּין וְזִיכָּה אֶת הַחַיָּיב,
phrases.english: if one judged a case and exonerated the one who was liable,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה (בכורות 28b), and it is talking about one judge ruling alone.

phrases.english: or made liable the one who was exempt,

phrases.aramaic: טִימֵּא אֶת הַטָּהוֹר, טִיהֵר אֶת הַטָּמֵא –
phrases.english: declared impure what was pure, or declared pure what was impure —
what he did is done,
and he pays from his own house.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the statement of רבי אבהו quoted in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's rule that fewer than three judges cannot make a valid ruling.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה says one judge's ruling stays in force. So fewer than three judges can make a valid ruling.

steps.title: Answer: the litigants accepted that judge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about litigants who agreed to accept this single judge.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where they accepted him upon themselves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי אבהו. It says the משנה is a special case where both sides agreed to be judged by this one person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The judge's ruling stands only because the litigants chose him, not because one judge makes a real court. Without that agreement, רבי אבהו's rule holds: fewer than three judges cannot rule.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (narrows the case)
That they accepted him upon themselves

phrases.english: Here, what are we dealing with?
A case where they accepted him upon themselves.
phrases.notes: 'They' are the two people in the court case, who agreed to have this one judge decide.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's challenge in step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה shows that a single judge's ruling is valid by itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ruling stands only because the litigants accepted the judge. Normally a court needs three.

steps.title: Challenge: then why does he pay?
steps.stepSummary: If the litigants agreed to accept his ruling, why should the judge have to pay for his mistake?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does he pay from his own house?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If both sides accepted the judge's decision, he should not owe anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Accepting a judge seems to mean accepting whatever he decides, even a mistake. If so, the judge should not be blamed for the loss. Yet the משנה says he pays, so the answer in step 5 seems incomplete.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
Why?

phrases.english: If so, why does he pay from his own house?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the litigants accepted the judge.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If they accepted his ruling, they accepted its result, so he should not have to pay.

steps.title: Answer: they asked him to judge by דין תורה
steps.stepSummary: The litigants accepted him on the condition that he judge by דין תורה. He failed to do that, so he pays.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because they said to him: judge for us by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the litigants' acceptance had a condition: they wanted a ruling by דין תורה. Since he got it wrong, he is responsible.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They did not accept any ruling at all. They accepted a correct ruling by Torah law. His ruling still stands, but he must pay for the loss because he did not deliver what they asked for.

keyTerms.meaning: Judge for us
Torah law

steps.whatToRemember: The single judge's ruling stands because the litigants accepted him. He pays because they asked for a correct דין תורה ruling and he made a mistake.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמְרוּ לֵיהּ: דָּיְינַתְּ לַן דִּין תּוֹרָה.
phrases.english: Because they said to him: judge for us according to Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמְרוּ לֵיהּ: דָּיְינַתְּ לַן דִּין תּוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adding a detail to the case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Accepting the judge means accepting any result, so he should not pay.
steps.terutzMaskana: They accepted him only to judge by דין תורה, so he pays for his mistake.

steps.title: רב ספרא asks: what kind of mistake?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא asks רבי אבא what kind of mistake the judge in the משנה made.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ספרא said to רבי אבא: he made a mistake in what?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא asks a clarifying question about the משנה רבי אבא quoted. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the mistaken ruling 'stays done'. But not every mistake lets a ruling stand. So רב ספרא wants to know what type of mistake the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: That he made a mistake
In what?

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סָפְרָא לְרַבִּי אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Safra said to Rabbi Abba:
Where he erred in what?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב סָפְרָא לְרַבִּי אַבָּא: דִּטְעָה בְּמַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the משנה from step 4 and asks about its case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of mistake the judge in the משנה made, such that his ruling still stands.

steps.title: It cannot be a mistake in an explicit משנה
steps.stepSummary: If the judge went against a clear משנה, his ruling would be cancelled, as רב ששת said in the name of רבי אמי. So that cannot be the case.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say he erred in something stated in a משנה, but רב ששת said in the name of רבי אמי: if he erred in a משנה matter, the ruling is reversed!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא tests one possible answer and rejects it. A mistake against a clear משנה does not 'stay done'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אמי rules that if a judge goes against an explicit משנה, the case goes back and the ruling is cancelled. But our משנה says 'what he did stays done'. So the judge in our משנה must have made a different kind of mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (offers a possibility to test)
In a matter stated in a משנה
Goes back; the ruling is reversed

phrases.english: If we say he erred in a matter of the Mishna,
phrases.notes: He means a clear, stated law, which the judge simply got wrong.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: but doesn't Rav Sheshet say in the name of Rabbi Ami:
if he erred in a matter of the Mishna, the ruling is reversed?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא דִּטְעָה בִּדְבַר מִשְׁנָה, וְהָאָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת אָמַר רַבִּי אַמֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first possible answer to step 8.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The possibility that the משנה is talking about a mistake against an explicit משנה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Such a ruling is reversed (חוזר), so it would not 'stay done'.

steps.title: It was a mistake in judgment
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a judge who made a mistake in weighing the matter (שיקול הדעת), not against a clear law.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, where he erred in his weighing of judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא gives the answer. The judge's mistake was in his reasoning or judgment call, so his ruling stays and he pays.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mistake against a clear משנה gets the ruling cancelled. A mistake in judgment is not obviously wrong in the same way, so the ruling stands. That explains why the judge must pay for the loss.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather
Weighing of judgment; a judgment call

steps.whatToRemember: Two kinds of judge's mistakes: in an explicit משנה, the ruling is reversed (חוזר). In שיקול הדעת, the ruling stands and the judge pays.
steps.whyThisMatters: This difference between טעה בדבר משנה and טעה בשיקול הדעת is a key rule in the laws of judges' mistakes.

phrases.english: Rather, where he erred in deliberation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the answer to step 8's question after step 9 ruled out the first option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The judge in the משנה made a mistake in שיקול הדעת, not against an explicit משנה.

steps.title: What exactly is a mistake in judgment?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a concrete case of a mistake in שיקול הדעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does a mistake in weighing the matter look like?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 10 said the judge erred in שיקול הדעת. Now the גמרא asks for a real example of what that means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know the mistake was not against a clear משנה, because that ruling would simply be cancelled. So the גמרא needs to explain what kind of error is less than that but still counts as a real mistake.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What does it look like?
Weighing the matter; a judge's judgment call

phrases.english: What is the case of a mistake in weighing the matter?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for a definition of the term introduced in Step 10
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A concrete definition of an error in שיקול הדעת

steps.title: רב פפא defines a judgment-call mistake
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא: when Sages argue with no final הלכה, and common practice follows one side but the judge followed the other, that is a mistake in שיקול הדעת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: For example, two תנאים or two אמוראים argue with each other. No final הלכה was stated for either side. The common practice follows one of them, and the judge went and ruled like the other. That is a mistake in weighing the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the definition. The judge did not break a clear law. He went against the accepted practice in an open argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since no official הלכה was stated, the judge's ruling has some backing and is not simply cancelled. But it goes against what everyone actually follows, so it still counts as a mistake. That is why the judge may have to pay.

keyTerms.meaning: Who argue with each other
The common practice; how people usually rule
According to the view of
Like the other one

steps.whatToRemember: A mistake in שיקול הדעת means ruling against the common practice in a dispute where no final הלכה was stated. It is not breaking a clear law.
steps.whyThisMatters: This definition explains when a judge's mistaken ruling stands and he pays, as opposed to when the ruling is simply cancelled.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
For example, two tanna'im or two amora'im
who disagree with each other,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא אִיתְּמַר הִלְכְתָא לָא כְּמָר וְלָא כְּמָר,
phrases.english: and the halacha was not stated like this Sage or like that Sage,
and the common practice follows one of them,
and he went and acted like the other one —
that is a mistake in weighing the matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: כְּגוֹן תְּרֵי תַנָּאֵי וּתְרֵי אָמוֹרָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Ruling against the common practice in an unresolved dispute between Sages

steps.title: Is the two-judge question an argument between תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: רבי מאיר says ביצוע needs three, and חכמים say פשרה can be done by one. It assumes everyone compares פשרה to דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say this is like an argument between תנאים: Making a compromise needs three judges, says רבי מאיר. The חכמים say a compromise can be done by one judge. They assumed that everyone compares compromise to judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier question of whether two judges can make a court. It is setting up a suggestion that the תנאים already argued about this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plan is this: if everyone says a compromise needs the same number of judges as a court case, then the argument about compromise also shows an argument about a court case. This step only lays out the ברייתא and that starting assumption. The actual suggestion comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say it is like an argument between תנאים
Making a compromise between the two sides
A compromise, instead of strict law
They assumed
We compare one thing to another

phrases.english: Let us say it is like a dispute of tanna'im:
Mediation is with three — the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say: compromise is even with a single judge.
They assumed that according to everyone
we compare compromise to judgment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the definition of שיקול הדעת and goes back to the dispute between שמואל and רבי אבהו (steps 1–3) about a court of two judges
steps.raayaObject: That the question of a court of two judges is an argument between תנאים

steps.title: So the argument is about judgment itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests רבי מאיר holds דין needs three, and חכמים hold דין can be done with two.
steps.simpleTranslation: Isn't this what they argue about? One Sage holds judgment needs three, and the other Sage holds judgment can be done with two?
steps.whatsHappening: Using the starting assumption from Step 13, the גמרא proposes what the argument is really about: how many judges a court case needs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If פשרה follows the same rules as דין, then רבי מאיר's 'three' means a court case needs three. The חכמים's smaller number would then show a court case can be done with fewer, such as two. This would make the two-judge question an old argument between תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: Isn't it that...? (a suggestion)
They argue about

phrases.english: Is it not that they argue about this,
that one Sage holds: judgment is with three,
and the other Sage holds: judgment is with two?
phrases.notes: The suggestion lines this up with the earlier argument: רבי מאיר matches רבי אבהו (three), and the חכמים match שמואל (two is enough).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the suggested conclusion from the setup in Step 13
steps.raayaObject: The תנאים argue whether דין needs three or two
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא, read with the assumption that פשרה is compared to דין

steps.title: No: everyone agrees judgment needs three
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion. Everyone agrees דין needs three. The real argument is whether פשרה is compared to דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Everyone agrees judgment needs three. Here they argue about this: one Sage holds we compare compromise to judgment, and the other Sage holds we do not compare compromise to judgment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof by dropping the assumption that everyone compares פשרה to דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on the assumption in Step 13. Now the גמרא says that assumption is exactly what they argue about. רבי מאיר compares פשרה to דין, so it needs three. The חכמים do not, so one judge is enough. So the ברייתא tells us nothing about a court of two.

keyTerms.meaning: According to everyone
A ruling by strict law, as opposed to a compromise

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying a court case can be done with one judge. They only say a compromise is different from a court case, so it does not need three.

phrases.english: No, for everyone agrees judgment is with three,
and here they argue about this:
that one Sage holds we compare compromise to judgment,
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר, who said compromise needs three.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר סָבַר לָא מַקְּשִׁינַן פְּשָׁרָה לְדִין.
phrases.english: and the other Sage holds we do not compare compromise to judgment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion of Step 14
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the ברייתא shows an argument about a court of two judges
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The assumption that everyone compares פשרה to דין is wrong; that comparison is the real argument

steps.title: Are there three opinions about compromise?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests there are three views of תנאים on פשרה: three judges, two, or one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say there are three opinions of תנאים about compromise: one Sage holds three, one Sage holds two, and one Sage holds one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices there seem to be three different numbers for פשרה. It suggests that each is a separate opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר says three and the חכמים say one. Another view holds two. If all three are real, separate opinions, then there is a three-way argument. The next step will check whether that is true.

keyTerms.meaning: Three opinions of תנאים
A single judge

phrases.english: Let us say: there are three tanna'im about compromise,
for one Sage holds with three,
and one Sage holds with two,
and one Sage holds with a single judge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the ברייתא's opinions to suggest a three-way argument
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the opinions requiring two and one for פשרה are really different

steps.title: Two judges are only for witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא (or רבי יימר בר שלמיא): the one who says two agrees one is enough. He wants two only so there are witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בריה דרב איקא said, and some say it was רבי יימר בר שלמיא: The one who says two holds that even one is fine. The reason he says two is so there will be witnesses to the compromise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea of three opinions. The 'two' view and the 'one' view really agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Two' is not a rule for making the compromise valid. It is a practical step, so there are witnesses who can confirm the terms later. So there are really only two opinions: רבי מאיר's three, and everyone else's one.

keyTerms.meaning: Even one is also fine
Witnesses

steps.whatToRemember: For פשרה, the opinion requiring two is not a third view. One judge is enough, and the second is only there as a witness.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא,
phrases.english: Rav Acha, son of Rav Ika, said,
and some say it was Rabbi Yeimar bar Shelamya:

phrases.aramaic: מַאן דְּאָמַר תְּרֵי – אֲפִילּוּ חַד נָמֵי,
phrases.english: The one who says two — even one is also fine,
and the reason that he says two —
is so that there will be witnesses to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דְּאָמַר תְּרֵי – אֲפִילּוּ חַד נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the three-opinion suggestion of Step 16
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects that there are three separate opinions about פשרה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'two' view is not a validity rule; the second person is only there as a witness

steps.title: רב אשי infers that compromise does not need a formal acquisition
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי learns from the view that ביצוע needs three judges that a פשרה does not need a קנין. If it did, the קנין would make it binding, and two judges would be enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Learn from this that a compromise does not need a קנין. If you thought it needed a קנין, then according to the one who says it needs three judges, why need three? Two should be enough, and the parties can make a קנין with each other!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי takes the earlier argument about how many judges a פשרה needs and pulls a new rule out of it: a פשרה does not need a קנין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קנין is a formal act that locks in a deal by itself. If a פשרה became binding through a קנין, the judges would not be what makes it binding, so there would be no reason for a full court of three. Since one view does demand three, the court itself must be what gives the פשרה its force, without any קנין.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from this. Used when drawing a conclusion from what was just said.
A formal act of acquisition that makes a deal or commitment legally binding.
If it entered your mind, meaning 'if you were to think that...'
Let it be enough.

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the judges make the קנין. He is saying that if a קנין were needed, it would do the binding work, so a court of three would be pointless.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ פְּשָׁרָה אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה קִנְיָן,
phrases.english: Learn from this that compromise does not require an act of acquisition,
for if it entered your mind that it requires an act of acquisition,

phrases.aramaic: לְמַאן דְּאָמַר צְרִיכָה – תְּלָתָא לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: then according to the one who says it requires [three], why do I need three?
phrases.notes: He means the view in the ברייתא that ביצוע needs three judges (step 13).

phrases.english: Let two be enough, and let one party make an acquisition from the other!

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ פְּשָׁרָה אֵינָהּ צְרִיכָה קִנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the debate about how many judges a פשרה needs and draws a new rule about קנין from it.
steps.raayaObject: That a פשרה does not need a קנין.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The view in the ברייתא that ביצוע needs three judges. That would be pointless if a קנין did the binding.

steps.title: The הלכה is that compromise does need an acquisition
steps.stepSummary: Even after רב אשי's inference, the גמרא rules that a פשרה does need a קנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: a compromise requires a קנין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final practical ruling: a פשרה needs a קנין to be binding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי showed what follows from the view that demands three judges. The final הלכה does not follow that line. In practice, a פשרה is only locked in once a קנין is made.

keyTerms.meaning: And the הלכה is. Introduces the final practical ruling.

steps.whatToRemember: רב אשי inferred that a פשרה does not need a קנין, but the final הלכה is that a פשרה does need a קנין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule: a settlement reached by compromise is not fully binding until a קנין is made.

phrases.english: And the halacha is: compromise requires an act of acquisition.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the practical ruling, which goes against רב אשי's inference.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A פשרה needs a קנין to be binding.

steps.title: A new ברייתא: mediation needs three judges just like judgment
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that just as דין is done by three judges, ביצוע is also done by three.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: Just as judgment is done by three, so mediation is done by three.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new section by quoting a ברייתא. It sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא puts ביצוע on the same footing as דין: both need three judges. This matches the view that compares פשרה to דין. The גמרא will now analyze this source.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too. Used to compare two cases.
Mediation, meaning settling a case by compromise.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Just as judgment is by three,
so mediation is by three.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהַדִּין בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה, כָּךְ בִּיצּוּעַ בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section with a new ברייתא after the previous discussion ended with a halachic ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ביצוע, like דין, requires three judges.
